title: Galaxy Z Fold8 Teardown: Who Makes the Hinge, FPCB and MLCCs
content:
We took the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 apart, part by part, and matched each part to the Korean listed company that makes that type of component. Hinge: S-Connect. Back plate: Fine M-Tec. Flexible circuit board: BH. Battery: Samsung SDI. Camera module and MLCCs: Samsung Electro-Mechanics. One caveat up front: none of these companies has disclosed that it supplies the Fold8 specifically. This is a map of who makes the parts, not a confirmed supplier list.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 (reconstruction image)

Teardown reconstruction video (not a physical disassembly)

Galaxy Z Fold8 teardown: seven parts

Exploded view of the Galaxy Z Fold8 (reconstruction image)

PartJobListed company that makes this partEvidence
HingeLets the phone foldS-Connect (KOSDAQ: 096630)Filing: makes foldable hinges
Back plateThin metal plate behind the folding screenFine M-Tec (KOSDAQ: 441270)Filing: makes mechanical parts for foldable displays
Flexible PCB (FPCB)Bendable circuit that links the two halvesBH (KOSDAQ: 090460)Filing: makes FPCBs
BatteryPowers the phoneSamsung SDI (KRX: 006400)Filing: makes small batteries for smartphones
Camera moduleLens, sensor and focus unit in oneSamsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150)Filing: makes smartphone camera modules
MLCCSmooths the power fed to chipsSamsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150)Filing: makes MLCCs
Foldable displayThe core of the phoneSamsung Display (unlisted)Not publicly traded

Read this before the table: each company above states in its Korean business report (DART) that it makes this type of part. We found no filing or announcement that any of them supplies the Galaxy Z Fold8 in particular. That is why we write "makes this part," not "supplier to the Fold8."

1. Hinge — S-Connect

The hinge that lets the Fold8 fold (reconstruction image)

The hinge is the joint that lets the screen fold in half. It has to survive hundreds of thousands of folds without letting the screen crease badly or the halves separate, which makes it one of the most precision-heavy parts in a foldable. S-Connect's business report lists foldable hinges among its products.

2. Back plate — Fine M-Tec

Metal back plate behind the folding screen (reconstruction image)

A folding screen is thin and fragile, so it needs a plate behind it. That plate has to flex along the fold and stay rigid everywhere else, which makes it hard to machine. Fine M-Tec's business report lists mechanical parts for foldable displays.

3. Flexible PCB — BH

Flexible circuit board crossing the fold (reconstruction image)

The two halves of a foldable move independently, so the circuit connecting them must bend. That is the job of a flexible printed circuit board. BH's business report lists FPCBs as its main product.

4. Battery — Samsung SDI

Battery (reconstruction image)

Foldables have large screens but must stay thin, so the battery is often split across both halves. Samsung SDI's business report lists small lithium-ion cells for smartphones.

5. Camera module — Samsung Electro-Mechanics

Camera module (reconstruction image)

A camera module packages the lens, image sensor and autofocus actuator into one unit. Samsung Electro-Mechanics lists smartphone camera modules in its business report.

6. MLCC — Samsung Electro-Mechanics

MLCCs packed on the board (reconstruction image)

MLCCs (multilayer ceramic capacitors) briefly store charge and release it evenly to keep chip voltages stable. Each is smaller than a grain of rice, and a smartphone uses hundreds to about a thousand of them. Samsung Electro-Mechanics is one of the world's largest MLCC makers.

7. Foldable display — Samsung Display (unlisted)

Foldable display (reconstruction image)

The most expensive and important part is the folding panel. Its maker, Samsung Display, is a subsidiary of Samsung Electronics and is not listed. Investors looking for "foldable display stocks" therefore end up looking at the materials and component makers around the panel, not the panel maker itself.

How to read foldable supply-chain stocks

The difference between a foldable and a regular phone is the fold. Parts that exist because of the fold (hinge, back plate, flexible circuits that cross the fold) are either unique to foldables or more expensive in them. Parts like batteries, camera modules and MLCCs go into every smartphone, so foldable sales alone move those companies' results much less. Separating these two groups is the first step when looking at "Galaxy Z Fold stocks."

FAQ

Which Korean stocks are linked to the Galaxy Z Fold8?
Listed Korean makers of the Fold8's part types include S-Connect (hinges), Fine M-Tec (back plates), BH (FPCBs), Samsung SDI (batteries) and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (camera modules, MLCCs). None has disclosed Fold8-specific supply.

Who makes foldable phone hinges in Korea?
S-Connect (KOSDAQ: 096630) lists foldable hinges in its business report.

Can I buy Samsung Display stock?
No. Samsung Display is unlisted; Samsung Electronics is its majority owner.

Is the video a real teardown?
No. It is a reconstruction based on public information.

Summary

  • Hinge: S-Connect (KOSDAQ: 096630)
  • Back plate: Fine M-Tec (KOSDAQ: 441270)
  • Flexible PCB: BH (KOSDAQ: 090460)
  • Battery: Samsung SDI (KRX: 006400)
  • Camera module and MLCC: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150)
  • Foldable display: Samsung Display (unlisted)

Sources: each company's business report filed with Korea's DART system (product descriptions).
The companies listed make these types of parts; they are not confirmed suppliers of the Galaxy Z Fold8. Images and video are reconstructions, not a physical teardown. This post summarizes public information and is not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
